summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant was admitted with headache, back pain, and poor appetite. He had been experiencing confusion and tremors, which were linked to elevated tacrolimus levels. An EEG confirmed encephalopathy likely due to medication toxicity. He underwent an ERCP for a biliary stricture, with successful placement of new stents. A urinary tract infection with Pseudomonas was treated with nitrofurantoin, and his kidney function improved. The patient was transitioned from tacrolimus to sirolimus, and his mental status stabilized. Due to ongoing mobility and self-care challenges, he was discharged to a rehabilitation facility with plans for close outpatient monitoring of medication levels and follow-up urine testing.
problems: Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of prostate
